# `Q-23-1` — Citeproc Resolves After Book Merge Point

> A book chapter orders the built-in `citeproc` filter into `.post`
> (after the `quarto` sentinel in `filters:`), so its citations
> resolve after this chapter pauses for project-wide
> crossref/bibliography aggregation.

## What this means

A multi-file HTML book renders every chapter through
Normalization → Crossref → Navigation, then pauses so a
project-wide crossref registry and a merged, deduplicated
bibliography can be built from every chapter's contribution before
any chapter resumes into Finalization. Harvesting a chapter's cited
references for that merge happens at the same pause point, right
after this chapter's own `citeproc` filter pass runs.

The `filters:` metadata key controls where each filter runs relative
to Quarto's own built-in processing, using the `quarto` sentinel:
filters listed before it run in `.pre` (before this pause point),
filters listed after it run in `.post` (after it). When `citeproc`
is ordered into `.post`, this chapter's citations are not resolved
yet when the pause happens — so its cited references are silently
missing from the book's merged bibliography, even though the
chapter's own in-text citations render normally later.

## Why this happens

- A chapter (or the project's shared `filters:` config) explicitly
  lists `citeproc` after the `quarto` sentinel — usually because a
  custom filter needs to run before citeproc and the whole list was
  written in one order without considering book-merge timing.

## How to fix

Move `citeproc` before the `quarto` sentinel in the `filters:` list
(in the chapter's own front matter, or the project's, whichever
declares it):

```yaml
filters:
  - citeproc
  - quarto
  - my-custom-filter.lua
```

If a custom filter genuinely needs to run *after* citeproc for a
single-document render, that ordering is not currently supported for
a book-merge or multi-file-HTML book chapter — citeproc must resolve
in `.pre` for this book's bibliography merge to see the chapter's
citations.
